name: maybe_Ui_MessageCmd_ShowRecordWithAttachmentB
summary: Inline-text command handler: reads the current row record through Ui_RowData_AtIndex from self+0x158, attaches the resource at 0x3B4F24 through the UI effect helper, pushes message command 3 and then displays the row record exactly like 0x002858D8 (same f_D6C/f_D70/f_D84 logic).
evidence: Re-read from decomp/readable/recovered: the two named callees Ui_RowData_AtIndex and maybe_Ui_Widget_ShowWithRecord plus Text_PushMessageByte(self,3) confirm a message-command handler, but the attachment target 0x3B4F24 and the difference from 0x003B4394 remain unidentified, so the 'B' variant stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveStartWindow_CreatePartB
signature: void* maybe_Ui_DiveStartWindow_CreatePartB(void* self, u32 recordHandle, u32 flag)
summary: Installs window vtable 0x75DD90, initialises the embedded sub-object at self+0xC, allocates a 0x4AC-byte part and constructs it with Ui_DiveStartWindowPart_Ctor, registers it via Ui_Object_CreatePartsFromTable, applies the record handle with Ui_DiveStartWindow_SetRecordHandle, marks the part active (+0x94=1) and runs its update slot +0x24.
evidence: Named Ui_DiveStartWindowPart_Ctor, Ui_Object_CreatePartsFromTable and Ui_DiveStartWindow_SetRecordHandle confirm the part construction, but the function also installs window vtable 0x75DD90 and has a second caller (maybe_Menu_TalkParty_CreatePanel), so whether it is a part factory or a window init-with-part cannot be settled from this body; kept as maybe_.

name: Ui_SakusenWindow_CreateWithIconState
summary: Allocates the 0x11D8-byte tactics window, constructs it with Ui_SakusenWindow_Ctor, registers it with the UI core, starts it, sets the active flag and applies Ui_Panel_UpdateStateIconFromList to initialise its state icons.
evidence: The ctor is the confident Ui_SakusenWindow_Ctor (0x2A3E78, also used by Ui_SakusenWindow_Create at 0x6D7160) and the 0x11D8 allocation matches that class, so the old generic 'Ui_CreateChildWidget_11D8' named the wrong class; this sibling is the one whose post-construction step is Ui_Panel_UpdateStateIconFromList.

name: Ui_SakusenWindow_CreateAndRefreshList
summary: Same Ui_SakusenWindow construction sequence as 0x002BBC3C, but the post-construction step is Ui_SakusenWindow_RefreshList, so the new window is created with its slot list already rebuilt.
evidence: Ctor Ui_SakusenWindow_Ctor is confident and this is one of its three identical factory wrappers; the only difference is the post-init call Ui_SakusenWindow_RefreshList. The old 'Ui_CreateChildWidget_11D8_State8' claimed an unbacked eight-state table and named the wrong class.

name: Ui_SakusenWindow_CreateWithMessageId
summary: Same Ui_SakusenWindow construction sequence as 0x002BBC3C, then Ui_SakusenWindow_InitPane is called with the owner's 16-bit message id (owner+0x4E) so the new window shows that message.
evidence: Ctor Ui_SakusenWindow_Ctor is confident; this wrapper is distinguished by Ui_SakusenWindow_InitPane(result, owner->f_4e). The old 'FromTextId' wording named a generic child widget rather than the SakusenWindow class.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_Ctor_53A8
summary: Tiny constructor stub: runs Ui_Object_CtorBase, installs vtable 0x771F70 and clears the pointer at +0x4C. It is one of the four sub-object constructors called by Ui_SakusenWindow_Ctor.
evidence: The only caller is the confident Ui_SakusenWindow_Ctor, so the object is a tactics-window child, but a vtable-only body cannot say which pane it is; the address-qualified name remains the honest level of detail.

name: maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_CtorPane
summary: Constructor of a tactics-window sub-pane: Ui_Object_CtorBase, vtable 0x773F20 and three cleared pointers at +0x4C..+0x58; paired with the deleting destructor 0x00479800.
evidence: Called only from the now-confident Ui_SakusenWindow_Ctor and paired with a destructor in the same family, so the tactics-window ownership is fixed; which of the several sub-panes it is cannot be read from a vtable-only body.

name: maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_CtorPaneB
summary: Smallest constructor stub of the tactics-window family: Ui_Object_CtorBase plus vtable 0x773FE8 and no other field initialisation; paired with destructor 0x00479B94.
evidence: Its only caller is Ui_SakusenWindow_Ctor and its dtor sits in the same vtable block, so the family is certain, but the pane role is unknowable from a two-instruction body.

name: maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_CtorSlotWidget
summary: Constructor of a tactics-window slot widget: shared Ui_Object constructor, class vtable 0x776E00 and default slot type 0x0B stored in the byte at +0x49.
evidence: Instantiated only by the confident Ui_SakusenWindow_Ctor, and the default type byte 0x0B is explicit, but what a type-0x0B slot means remains unknown, so the descriptive name stays a maybe_.

name: Field_SpriteObject_InitFromShortRecord
summary: Initialises a field sprite object from a packed placement record: resolves the sprite core with Gfx_SpriteActor_CreateFromTable, stores the record's model/size/priority fields, builds the colour animator and span child and attaches the billboard.
evidence: The named caller Field_SceneSpawnBlock_EffectEmitterAndActor and the named callees Gfx_SpriteActor_CreateFromTable, Field_SceneObject_SetModelSize, Gfx_CreateFColAnimator and Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChild all match field sprite-object construction; the 'short record' name correctly describes the 11-halfword placement record it reads.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_SnapToNearbyActor
summary: Walks the scene object's linked list for the entry with class tag 0x7C4D9C; when that entry is not at the same position, moves this gimmick's model to the entry's x/y/z via Model_SetMeshById and then either calls Field_SceneObject_SetModelSize or 0x5F2F4C according to the entry's +0xD4 flag.
evidence: Model_SetMeshById and Field_SceneObject_SetModelSize are now named and are called with the other object's coordinates, which supports the snap-to-object reading, but there is still no caller and the +0xD4 choice is unexplained.

name: maybe_Model_Actor_UpdateScale
summary: Re-applies the actor's model size from its f_78/f_7C dimensions and selects the visual scale: for overlay modes 1..4 it uses the fixed default scale constants, otherwise the Field2D visual state supplies the per-character scale and an update flag chooses between two globals.
evidence: Named Field_SceneObject_SetModelSize and the Field2D helpers confirm the scale source and the mode test (UI overlay +0x27F), but the VFP return is lost into in_s0/in_s4 in the decompiler output, so the exact value flow remains damaged and the name stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Save_MigrateAllSlots
summary: Mounts the save data archive (shared handle 0x72D780, name 'data:') and loops over the four slots: writes each slot's strings with Save_WriteSlotStrings, validates two stored markers and the two 0x5E magic bytes, then copies the slot header fields into the per-slot record and sets the slot state (1/2 ok, 3/4 failure, 6/7 abort).
evidence: The named Save_WriteSlotStrings plus the four-slot loop and 0x5E markers make the slot-initialisation role clear, but nothing in the new names proves this is a version migration rather than first-time slot initialisation, so the 'Migrate' wording stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Save_MigrateVerify
summary: Verification half of the save-slot setup: mounts the same 'data:' archive, loads the slot header with slot 0xFFFFFFFF, reads the marker at save+0x1820 and compares save->f_1828 and the f_182C checksum with the 0x5E magic; writes result state f_E3C0 = 1 (ok), 4 (already done) or 3 (failed) and sub-state f_E3C4 = 3/4/6/7.
evidence: Its callee is now the named Save_LoadSlotHeader and its caller is the save task resolver maybe_Save_LoadTask_ResolveObject, which confirms it verifies saved slot data; whether the operation is a migration or an ordinary load check is still not proven.

name: maybe_Ui_Panel_HandleInput
summary: Per-frame input handler for a selectable panel: reacts to the menu cursor, plays error SE 0xEC0 and BGM 0x2E when the last slot is selected with no valid target, and drives the panel state machine with state 7 (accept) or 8 (back).
evidence: The named callees Menu_Cursor_HasTarget, maybe_Ui_Slot_IsLast, Sound_PlaySeById and Snd_RequestBgmPlay confirm input handling, but the old 'JockeyPanel' class name has no support (no caller, no named vtable sibling), so it is replaced by the honest generic panel name.

name: maybe_Ui_AnimWidget_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a small shared UI widget: builds the base through Ui_WindowBase_Ctor, installs vtable 0x77BF90 and attaches one child through 0x1A6768; used by both Ui_SetupSwapWindow and Ui_SetupRenkeiWindow.
evidence: Named caller Ui_SetupRenkeiWindow and the vtable/base ctor confirm a widget constructor, but vtable 0x77BF90 has no named sibling and the child helper is still unnamed, so 'animation widget' remains a description rather than a proven class name.

name: Ui_BattleBindWindow_CtorA
summary: Constructor of the 0x8C-byte battle 'win_bind' window: base-constructs through Ui_WindowBase_Ctor, installs vtable 0x7698A4 and clears the seven state words at +0x70..+0x88.
evidence: Ui_BattleWindow_CreateMainWindow allocates exactly 0x8C bytes, binds the object to the pane 'win_bind' and calls this variant when battle work +0x4244 is 0 (the other variant 0x003D2488 is used when it is non-zero), which fixes both the class and the A/B split.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_ApplySetupResult
signature: void maybe_Field_Actor_ApplySetupResult(FieldActor* actor, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Damaged Thumb copy of the field-actor action-init sequence: Field_NpcApplyActionResult, position copy through Ui_Overlay_GetTargetDrawPos3D, vtable+0x84 animation, Map_PlaceObject and the scaled-speed lookup. Duplicates 0x003D8D74.
evidence: Comparison with the now-readable 0x003D8D74 shows the same call sequence, but unaff_r4/r7 and in_s0 in the body mean the register flow is lost; the action-init reading is preferred over 'apply setup result' only as a summary, and the name stays a maybe_.

name: Gfx_SpriteChild_AppendNamedFlagsFromTable
signature: u32 Gfx_SpriteChild_AppendNamedFlagsFromTable(void* childFlags, u32 nameHash, u32 row)
summary: Variant of 0x003DF9AC that takes the flag bits from the 13-entry table at 0x72537C indexed by the row argument; validates the name hash against the intern table and appends the (hash,bits) pair to the sprite child's 32-entry list before OR-ing the bits into its scene sprite entry.
evidence: The callers are named Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChild / Field_Object2D_CreateSpriteEntry, the callees Gfx_GetSceneSpriteContext and Gfx_Scene_AddSpriteEntrySmall are named, and the 'self' argument is &spriteChild->f_3c (not a UI object), so the old 'Ui_SetNamedFlagFromTable' prefix named the wrong subsystem.

name: Gfx_SpriteChild_AppendNamedFlags
signature: u32 Gfx_SpriteChild_AppendNamedFlags(void* childFlags, u32 nameHash, u32 bits, u32 key)
summary: Validates a name hash against the global intern table and, when the sprite child still has room (f_128 < 0x20), appends the (hash,bits) pair to its 32-entry list and ORs the bits into the target scene sprite entry's +8 word.
evidence: The named caller Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChild passes &spriteChild->f_3c, params+4 and tmpl->f_44, and the callees Gfx_GetSceneSpriteContext / Gfx_Scene_AddSpriteEntrySmall are named; this is sprite-child render flags, not a UI flag, so 'Ui_' was the wrong prefix.

name: Battle_CalcSpellEffectTotal
signature: int Battle_CalcSpellEffectTotal(u32 spellId, void* row, u32 target, float scale, u32 arg5, int applyLayout, int arg7)
summary: Evaluates a spell's eight 0x2C-byte effect entries (row kind 5) against a target, sums their values with the RNG variance, and when the spell's +0x296 flag is clear instead lays out the eight default rows; writes the resulting short to row+4.
evidence: The function starts with the spell-record resolver 0x0018C184 (SpellRecord per FACTS) and the callees Battle_MonsterUI_Dispatch / Battle_MonsterUi_ResolveRowType resolve the effect rows; its position in 0x00485D90..0x00497900 (Battle Combat Math) and the old 'Text_' prefix was wrong.

name: Battle_CalcSkillParamValue
signature: int Battle_CalcSkillParamValue(void* out, const void* param, void* owner)
summary: Computes a skill-derived combat value from a weapon/ability parameter record: if the record has an extra id it rolls base +/- variance around that sub-record, otherwise it selects skill 0x4E/0x4F/0x50 from the parameter type 0x94/0x96/0x97 and interpolates between the skill record's min and max fields, finally clamping and returning a short.
evidence: The named caller Ui_Status_CalcWeaponAttackValue passes the record returned by func_00639C98(member, 0x94/0x96) as 'param' and stores the result in the displayed attack field; the body resolves SkillRecord ids through 0x0018C1B8 (SkillRecord wrapper per FACTS) and switches on the same 0x94/0x96/0x97 ids, so the old 'ItemDamage' name was wrong.

name: Battle_CalcSpellRowValue
signature: int Battle_CalcSpellRowValue(u32 spellId, void* row, const void* param, void* owner)
summary: Single-row companion of Battle_CalcSpellEffectTotal: resolves the spell record for spellId, picks param->f_18/f_1C (or their min/max for row kind 0x12) according to the spell row-kind byte +0x2A, adds the RNG variance, clamps at zero and stores the short in row+4.
evidence: Both named callers (Ui_Status_CalcWeaponAttackValue and Battle_ActionSequence_SetTurnTiming) pass a spell id plus the record from func_00639C98; the spell-record resolver 0x0018C184 and the row-kind switch show this is battle spell-row math, so the old 'Text_CalcRowValueFromActor' prefix was wrong.

name: maybe_Battle_CalcSkillParamValueEx
signature: int maybe_Battle_CalcSkillParamValueEx(void* out, const void* param, void* owner)
summary: Battle-time twin of Battle_CalcSkillParamValue: resolves skill 0x4E/0x4F/0x50 from the parameter type, interpolates the skill record's min/max fields with an RNG variance and returns the short value; called while a member's queued battle actions execute.
evidence: The body is the same math as 0x0048A63C and its only caller is the named Battle_ActionSequence_ExecuteMemberActions; the 'Ex' suffix only records that this is the action-execution entry into the same calculation, so the specific role stays a maybe_.

name: Battle_Unit_RefreshDisplayValues
summary: Refreshes a battle unit's displayed numbers: resolves the unit's party-member record, checks the enemy display slot and marks the layout dirty when it changed, converts the member's +0x740/+0xEC0/+0xB00 values to floats for the message rows and returns the (f_B00, f_EC0) pair.
evidence: The named caller Battle_Monster_UpdateMpBar and callees Battle_Enemy_GetDisplaySlot, Text_MarkLayoutDirty and Text_UpdateBlinkStateH confirm this is the display-refresh side of the unit widget; the three func_0035EB98 lookups are party-member records per FACTS.

name: maybe_Camera_RegularShakeKeyData
summary: Not a function: 0x00591204 is a .rodata blob holding the word 0x0046B5A4, the ASCII key 'ReguralyShake' (0x00591207-0x00591215) and the float 0xBF800000. The readable C is the decompiler mis-decoding that data and folding in the real function that starts at 0x0059121C.
evidence: The disassembly shows `pop {pc}` ending the previous function at 0x00591200, then the ASCII bytes of 'ReguralyShake' and the float, and `push {r4,lr}` at 0x0059121C; this entry is a data blob, which is why no code-level name can be confirmed.

name: Camera_CreateRegularShakeWork
summary: Creates the camera 'ReguralyShake' work object: allocates 0x94 bytes, constructs it with vtable 0x591360 via Container_NameHash_Ctor, copies the five float parameters from s0-s4, stores the slot byte at +0x24 and inserts it into the camera named map at game work +0x78.
evidence: The callee/vtable pair is now named Camera_RegularShake_Ctor (vtable 0x591360) and the named-map insert uses the 'ReguralyShake' key at 0x00591204; the Gfx_RegularShake family at 0x00591860 is a separate object, so the 'B' suffix is unnecessary and the Camera_ class is proven.

name: Ui_ObjectList_DestroySlotsB
summary: Destructor body of the 3+2-slot Ui_ObjectList variant (vtable 0x783D04): installs the class vtable, releases both reference pairs, releases the three slots at +5 and the two at +0x95, and runs std_destroy_range over both slot arrays.
evidence: std_destroy_range is the verified array-destructor helper (0x00100BE0 destroys backwards through a dtor), and the release helpers are Ui_ObjectList_ReleaseRefPairA/B, so this is destruction, not the 'CtorA' construction the first pass assumed; the only caller is Field_UiGimmick_Dtor.

name: Ui_ObjectList_DestroySlotsC
summary: Destructor body of the ten-slot Ui_ObjectList variant (vtable 0x783D14): clears the list, releases and destroys the ten 0x30-byte entries at +0x22, resets the index to 0xFF and destroys the 10 x 0xC0 slot array.
evidence: The body ends in std_destroy_range (0x00100BE0, the verified array destructor) over 10 slots and its only caller is Field_UiGimmick_Dtor, so 'CtorB' was wrong; the ten-slot layout distinguishes it from the 3+2 and 3-slot variants.

name: Ui_ObjectList_DestroySlotsD
summary: Destructor body of the three-slot Ui_ObjectList variant (vtable 0x783D24): installs the vtable, runs Ui_ObjectList_DestroyEntries as the reset and destroys the three 0xC0-byte slots at +6 with std_destroy_range.
evidence: std_destroy_range is the verified destructor helper, the slot count is three and the only caller is Field_UiGimmick_Dtor; the first pass's 'CtorC' label described a construction that the body does not perform.

name: maybe_Ui_ObjectList_UpdateSlotOrder
signature: void maybe_Ui_ObjectList_UpdateSlotOrder(UiObjectList* self, int base, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Rebuilds the ten visible list slots after a scroll: walks the 10 entries (stride 0xC0 from +0x88), computes each new index from the list index at +0x808 and the direction, releases the old entry and re-creates it through 0x30B120.
evidence: The Ghidra body hits 'bad instruction data' and halt_baddata() and uses unaff_r8, so the register flow is only partly recovered; the named callers Ui_ObjectList_SwapOrder / Field_Gimmick_RebuildRows still support the slot-order reading, but confidence must stay low.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_HidePartsAndNotify
summary: Walks the gimmick's part list, hides each part through its vtable slot +0xA4 and spawns the matching effect, then raises the field's render part count to at least 2, updates both UI panels with colour 0xEEEEEE00 and plays SE 0xE46.
evidence: Field_Gimmick_FindSlotObjectById and Sound_PlaySeById are named and the part iteration is explicit, but the vtable slot +0xA4(6,4) and the two panel slots +0x44/+0x20 are still undecoded, so 'hide' remains an interpretation.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_InitSlotEffects
summary: Resets and fills the gimmick's eight 0x14-byte slot records: clears the counters, writes the empty-handle sentinel, binds each slot to a part object found by Field_Gimmick_FindSlotObjectById and assigns randomised start/end ticks from the game RNG, then copies the per-part values into the two model objects.
evidence: The named Field_Gimmick_FindSlotObjectById plus the explicit 8-slot/0x14-stride clear and the RNG-derived timing fields make the initialisation clear, but 'effects' is still inferred from the later slot consumers rather than proven here.

name: Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_UpdatePresets
summary: Per-frame update of a scene sprite set's two layers: interpolates the first layer's cloud colours with Field_Sky_InterpolateCloudColors, blends the second layer's presets with Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_BlendPresets when f_35 is clear, and only under debug global 0x7A68E0 appends the active slot ids to a diagnostic string.
evidence: Both main callees are now named (Field_Sky_InterpolateCloudColors and Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_BlendPresets) and the named caller Ui_SceneFlow_Update drives it per frame; the diagnostic string is behind the debug flag, so the old 'BuildDebugString' named a side effect.

name: Gfx_UpdateDisplayStateB
summary: Variant of the display-command frame step used when a new command block must be acquired: selects a free/busy block with Svc_QuerySessionInfoLocked, re-sends through Svc_RequestWithRetry or waits and sends through Svc_WaitReadyAndSendRequest, then restores the pending flag.
evidence: All callees are GPU command-stream functions (Svc_QuerySessionInfoLocked, Svc_RequestWithRetry, Svc_WaitReadyAndSendRequest, Gfx_LockedIpcCmd3E0080) and the caller is Engine_DispatchFrameCallbacks; 'Snd_' was wrong because nothing here touches the sound driver.

name: Gfx_UpdateDisplayState
summary: One frame step of the GPU display-command state machine: if the pending byte at 0x7AE954 is set it stops the current sequence, advances the state, notifies the registered callback (+0x38), then either waits for readiness or sends the request and restores the flag.
evidence: The named callees Gfx_LockedIpcCmd3E0080, Svc_WaitReadyAndSendRequest, Gfx_WaitForIpcIdle and maybe_Gfx_NegotiateDisplayMode all belong to the display/GSP command path, and the only caller is Engine_DispatchFrameCallbacks, so the 'Snd_' prefix was a misnomer.

name: maybe_Os_SetThreadPriorityMode
summary: Maps a small mode word onto the scheduler/GPU helpers: 0 -> helper(3) plus Gfx_LockedIpcCmd3E0080(0), 1 -> helper(2) plus Gfx_LockedIpcCmd3E0080(1), 2 -> helper(1) only; other values are ignored.
evidence: The disassembly shows the 0/1/2 -> 3/2/1 remapping and the two callees (0x113A40 and Gfx_LockedIpcCmd3E0080) are now named, but which hardware mode 0x113A40 programs is still unidentified, so neither 'thread priority' nor a display-only reading is proven.

name: maybe_Gfx_IsDisplayStateReady
summary: Returns true when the display state machine reports state 1 from 0x0010CC10; Engine_DispatchFrameCallbacks tests it as the first gate before running the frame step.
evidence: The caller Engine_DispatchFrameCallbacks and the sibling 0x00107AE8 (both Gfx_ neighbours) fix the subsystem, but 0x0010CC10 itself is still unnamed, so 'state 1 means ready' is only the most plausible reading.

name: maybe_Gfx_IsDisplayStateActive
summary: Returns true when either display state source (0x0010CC20 or 0x00113A00) is non-zero; Engine_DispatchFrameCallbacks tests it immediately after 0x00107AD4 as the second frame gate.
evidence: The named caller Engine_DispatchFrameCallbacks pairs it with the other Gfx display gate and both state getters are used by the GPU command pump, so the Gfx_ prefix is supported; the exact state meaning is still unknown, keeping the confidence below 0.5.

name: Svc_Cfg_EnsureService
signature: u32 Svc_Cfg_EnsureService(u8* kindOut, u32 second, u16* resultOut)
summary: Makes sure one of the three config sessions is usable: tries the refcounted cfg:u acquire, then cfg:s, then cfg:i, writing which one succeeded (0/1/2) to kindOut; that kind is the same value the release dispatcher 0x0011212C consumes.
evidence: The named callees Svc_Cfg_AcquireService, Svc_Cfg_OpenServiceS and Svc_Cfg_OpenServiceI plus the caller Os_AcquireSharedSession confirm an acquire/ensure helper, and the old 'Os_ReleaseSharedSessionEx' claimed the opposite operation. The unaff_r4 in the tail is a damaged-decompilation artifact of the refcount release helper and does not affect the acquire dispatch, whose three open/acquire calls and kind outputs are intact in the disassembly.

name: maybe_Svc_Ir_SetupChannel
signature: u32 maybe_Svc_Ir_SetupChannel(u32 service, u32 buffer, int first, u32 width, int c, u32 height, u32 mode)
summary: Opens the shared ir:USER session on first use, maps the shared memory, sends the channel setup request (coordinates and sizes in 8.8 fixed point) and initialises the endpoint, cleaning up on failure.
evidence: The service-name literal at 0x754FC0 was verified as the bytes 'ir:USER', so the IR session reading is solid, but the surrounding callees still carry Snd_ names (Snd_SetChannelMatrix, maybe_Snd_SetChannelOutput) and the exact request format is unidentified, so the role stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Svc_Ir_CloseService
summary: Closes the shared ir:USER session opened by 0x00122200: sends the 0x00020000 close command, closes the shared-memory handle, releases the session handle, unmaps the shared memory and clears the open flag.
evidence: It is the exact inverse of 0x00122200 - same globals (open flag 0x7B2D08, session 0x7B2D2C, shared memory 0x7F2DE0) whose open call uses the verified 'ir:USER' literal; the old 'Gfx_FinalizeSession' name claimed a GPU session, which the string contradicts.

name: maybe_Svc_SyncObject_DestroyB
summary: Destroys the second kind of synchronisation object: closes its kernel handle with Os_CloseHandle, then closes the remaining handle with svcCloseHandle and clears the stored handle field; returns the object.
evidence: The sibling 0x00509A20 has the same shape with a different close helper and both are waited on together by the content-cache code at 0x0050A714; which primitive each object kind represents (event vs condition) is still unknown.

name: maybe_Gfx_Sprite_SetupPattern
signature: uint32_t maybe_Gfx_Sprite_SetupPattern(Sprite* sprite, const uint8_t* patternTable)
summary: Parses a compact 2D pattern table (node tags 0x82/0x85/0x8E carry a size pair, a flip bit and a pattern id), maps the id through the 14-entry flip permutation and applies the frame descriptor to the sprite's renderer.
evidence: The tag tests and the 14-entry permutation are visible and the callers are sprite/UI setup routines, but the node walk uses unaff_r7 after Ghidra lost the entry register, so the body is damaged and the pattern-table reading cannot be raised above a maybe_.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_RowTransition_Tail
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_Ui_RowTransition_Tail(u32 arg1, int arg2, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Thumb fragment at the end of a battle state handler: walks 0x12-byte row records comparing word 0, resolves an action row through Game_GetDataManager and updates the message object at +0x260/+0x7A4; probably the tail of 0x00483870 rather than a function of its own.
evidence: The entry is Thumb while its neighbours are ARM, it has no prologue, and the body reads unaff_r4/r5/r6/r7/r9, so the symbol boundary is damaged; the 0x12 stride still matches the row records of Battle_PartyMember_Update (0x00483870), but the entry point itself is not trustworthy.

name: Battle_PartyMember_UpdateRevive
summary: Revive-state handler of a battle party-member display object: when the state counter reaches 0x172 it posts Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnRevive and plays SE 0x128, waits for the sound handle, then adds state flags 2 and advances the display object.
evidence: The now-named callee Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnRevive (whose other callers are Battle_ActorAction_ShowRevivePopup and Battle_UpdateUnitDisplay) plus the 0x172/0x17D state counters identify this as the revive animation state; the old 'UpdateEnter' wording had no support for an enter/battle-start role.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_PlayReactionThunk
signature: void maybe_Field_Gimmick_PlayReactionThunk(void* self, int arg2, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: 36-byte Thumb callback: builds a reaction matrix from the part's +0x224, calls the UI effect hook when self->f_E8 is set and plays sound id 300.
evidence: The fragment is only three calls long and uses unaff_r4/r6/r7 (damaged register flow), so the matrix-build and UI-hook callees cannot be confirmed; the thunk role is visible but 'reaction' remains an interpretation.

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_PlayFrameSounds
summary: Frame-driven sound/state player: increments the frame counter at +0x14, plays SE 0xE5F at frame 5 and 0xE60 at frame 25, calls the 0x4A43CC hook at frame 35 and after frame 44 copies a vtable/handle pair from the 0x72A79C data block.
evidence: The frame comparisons and the two SE ids are explicit, but there is still no caller and only the sound helpers are named, so the 'Overlay' owner is a guess from the 0x72A79C data block.

name: maybe_Sound_FadeTimer_Get
summary: Returns a BGM fade time window: while a fade is pending it triggers the fade (UI core +0x1C slot, Sound_GetPlayer, 0x001EE018) and returns the short window from 0x72BD64, otherwise the default window from the same global table.
evidence: The body only selects between two pairs of globals under a pending-fade flag and calls the sound helper; with no caller and only Sound_GetPlayer/Ui_GetCore named, the fade-timer reading remains unconfirmed.

name: maybe_Ui_StopFadeAndSound
summary: Stops a pending fade and its sound: calls the UI core +0x14 fade helper, the sound-player stop helper and then the cleanup routine 0x0029126C on self+4's +0x133C field.
evidence: Ui_GetCore and Sound_GetPlayer are the only named callees and there is still no caller or vtable slot, so the 'Shop' owner from the first pass is replaced by the honest Ui_ prefix; what exactly 0x002D24BC and 0x0029126C stop is not identified.
